script: I confessed love after she'd already moved on—her reply shattered me.. I was at the gym in October and met this girl who worked in the same industry as me. We hit it off instantly; she was shy, introverted, and confessed she had a hard time talking to people. We'd chat for hours, so I got to know her pretty well in a month or two. I started liking her. I never told her how I felt. Her birthday was in December, so I was planning to ask her out around then. She stopped coming to the gym for a while, so I didn't see her the whole month. In January I ran into her at work, and she said she'd started going earlier. I assumed she'd figured out I was interested but didn't feel the same, so she'd changed her schedule to avoid me. (Low self‑esteem, right?) In March she told me she'd met another guy in February and they're getting along. I panicked. I checked her socials, asked to follow her, and she blocked me. I thought she'd known I liked her all along and just wanted to keep her distance. Fast forward to yesterday. I saw her at the gym after months. She was talking about her new boyfriend. They've been on weekend trips, just booked a trip to Switzerland for an Ironman. I finally told her how I'd felt. "I am glad we're catching up. I know you probably suspected I liked you back around November and didn't feel the same, but please don't think you need to distance yourself from me because of that." She looked surprised. "To be honest, you've majorly overthought me changing gym times. I did that because it was getting too busy, not because of you. I had no idea you liked me. I never got those vibes from you. You're always chatty and friendly with everyone, so I assumed that's how you were being with me. You've kind of outed yourself there." I said, "Damn it, I should've just kept my mouth shut. Although I suppose the answer would've still been no anyway so no love lost?" She replied, "I wouldn't say that. I was single then, so I don't know how I would've answered. Maybe I'd have said yes." My heart sank. I told her, "don't say that" because I'd rather know I never had a chance than be left wondering what could've been. I think she heard the pain in my voice; I didn't do a good job of hiding it. She said, "It's hard to say how I'd have responded at the time. Things were different. I think we were both just bad communicators. I was shy and thought you were just being friendly, and it seems you misread my shyness as lack of interest." Now my head is all over the place. Since January I convinced myself she'd known I liked her and simply wasn't interested. So even though seeing her with someone else was painful, I never thought I had a chance anyway. Now I know she never realized I liked her in the first place. I can't stop thinking about how things could have been different if I'd told her sooner. I am wondering if she's just being kind now that she's happy, or if we really just misread each other. I'll never know for sure, but I can't stop thinking about it. Has anyone else had something similar happen where you found out months or years later that the other person had completely misunderstood your intentions? How did you get over it and move on?
